deep.reconstruction:
This page is printed, not handwritten. It is p. 14 of an elementary German arithmetic textbook set in Fraktur, part of the chapter on common fractions (§§30–34). Gauss's only handwriting here is on the facing leaf at the right edge, which is cut off. Those notes continue onto the next folio. They show the falling-factorial notation d[n]/dx and ∫[n]dx, and a column of decimals (0.323…, 1.302…, 0.869…, 0.871…, 1.312…, 0.334…, sum 5.014…; a struck-through 1.00…; then 0.5014). On the next page these belong to quadrature-type numerical work (including a dx/(1−…)^{1/2} integral), alongside approximations of l2 = ln 2. They are not part of this page's content.

The printed content:

(§30, case 1: integer multiplier) (3/4)·6 = 18/4. Interpreted as repeated addition, this is 3/4 added six times, which equals (3·6)/4 (§10). Cancelling the common factor 2 (§19) gives (3·3)/2 = 9/2.

(§30, case 2: fractional multiplier) Rule: (a/b)·(n/m) = an/(bm). Derivation:
- Put A = a/b and B = n/m.
- By the definition of a quotient (§15), a = bA and n = mB.
- Multiplying these, using commutativity and associativity (§17.2, §12), gives an = bm·AB.
- Dividing by bm gives an/(bm) = AB, the required product.
- Example: (3/4)(5/6) = 15/24 (left unreduced; it equals 5/8).

(§31: division of fractions) Method: bring dividend and divisor to a common denominator, then divide the numerators.
- Integer divisor: (3/4):6 = (3/4):(24/4) = 3/24 = 1/8.
- Integer dividend: 6:(3/4) = (24/4):(3/4) = 24/3 = 8.
- Both fractions: (3/5):(2/7) = (21/35):(10/35) = 21/10 = 2 + 1/10.

(§32) The product rule can be re-derived from the division rule: (a/b)(n/m) = (a·n/m):b = (an/m):(bm/m) = an/(bm).

(§33) Definition of reducing a fraction to lowest terms by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor. Example from §27: 45/120 = (3·15)/(8·15) = 3/8.
errors: No mathematical errors in the printed text. All arithmetic checks out.
15/24 is left unreduced (= 5/8). This is a matter of style, not an error.
The final term of the repeated sum 3/4+…+3/4 in the first line is poorly printed or ambiguous in the image; mathematically it must be 3/4.

transcription_corrections: The page body is a printed Fraktur textbook page, not Gauss's handwriting. Only the cut-off notes at the right edge (facing leaf) are manuscript.
§32 is printed as 'Der 2te Fall §. 30 kann auch nach §. 31. 1. behandelt werden'. The mark after '30' in the image is a stray blemish.
The heading of §31 reads 'Einen Bruch mit einer gegebenen Zahl zu dividiren' ('Zahl' is partly damaged in the image).
